newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton prices extend gains on low arrivals.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton prices extend gains on low arrivals.

text.p: Indian cotton prices on Friday extended gains though fresh mill buying remained slow, dealers said.
Limited arrivals and a shortage of ready stock particularly of medium and superior quality dragged prices up, they said.
Market talk that state-owned agencies may hike selling prices due to sliding supplies also prompted speculative interest for cotton in the open market, a broker said.

In spot deals Bengal-deshi rose by five rupees at 900/940 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) while Punjab saw-ginned rose by 25 rupees at 1,625/1,700 rupees per maund and F-414 lifted by 10/30 rupees at 1,930/1,945 rupees per maund.

Daily average arrivals of cotton in the Punjab region had dropped to 1,000/1,500 bales (170 kg each). Gujarat Kalyan (medium-staple) also moved up by 200 rupees at 13,900/14,200 rupees per candy (355.56 kg) amid a shortage of ready stock.
